summary: For containerized installs, put `postgresql_admin_password`, `gateway_admin_password`, `gateway_pg_password`, `controller_admin_password`, `controller_pg_password`, `hub_admin_password`, `hub_pg_password`, `eda_admin_password`, `eda_pg_password` (and `registry_password` when connected) in the vault and run `ansible-playbook ansible.containerized_installer.install -e @vault.yml --ask-become-pass`, without repeating those variables in the plaintext inventory.
questions: How do I use a vault file with the containerized installer?
Which passwords go in the vault for containerized AAP?
Can I keep passwords in both the inventory and the vault?

answer_card.title: Containerized install with a vault file
answer_card.answer_md:
`vault.yml` holds:
```yaml
postgresql_admin_password: <secure_password>
gateway_admin_password: <secure_password>
gateway_pg_password: <secure_password>
controller_admin_password: <secure_password>
controller_pg_password: <secure_password>
hub_admin_password: <secure_password>
hub_pg_password: <secure_password>
eda_admin_password: <secure_password>
eda_pg_password: <secure_password>
registry_password: <secure_cdn_password>  # connected installs
```
Run from the install directory:
```bash
ansible-playbook ansible.containerized_installer.install -e @vault.yml --ask-become-pass
```
The guide prints this command; an encrypted file also needs the vault password (for example `--ask-vault-pass`). Don't duplicate these variables in the inventory.
